clue.text: On the rocks, in the sun and air

parts.note: taken as written
Sol is the Latin name for the sun
to vent something is to air it, give it expression

explanation.surface: Someone lounging on the rocks, out in the sun and fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' looks like a seaside spot but means bankrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: A business on the rocks is failing financially, unable to pay its debts.

clue.text: People are clapped in these clubs

definitions.meaning: prisoners were 'clapped in' leg fetters and chains
golf clubs with metal heads, numbered three to nine

explanation.surface: Applause for people, as if at a club night.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetters are metal shackles, and golfers carry metal-headed clubs of the same name.

clue.text: Is stout perhaps, so doesn't dance

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words Is stout could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A plump person declines to take to the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of IS STOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay seated while others take the floor is the idiom for skipping a dance.

clue.text: I'm fired about restrictive practice

indicators.note: about places the first piece round the second, enclosing it

parts.note: something fired, set alight, is lit
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone sacked over a restrictive practice at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' suggests dismissal, but it means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: A restriction or cap on what is allowed is a boundary set in practice.

clue.text: Draws dissected Eastern insect

indicators.note: cut up in a lab, so the word insect is taken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A biology student sketching an oriental insect cut open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draws' looks like sketching, but it means lures. 'dissected' rearranges INSECT into NTICES.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw someone in is to lure or tempt them.

clue.text: What figures neat girls may display

indicators.note: the letters of neat girls may be laid out to show a different word

explanation.surface: Tidy young women showing off their figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'display' rearranges NEAT GIRLS. 'figures' suggests body shape but means geometric shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-sided shapes are geometric figures.

clue.text: It needs a key first for opening

indicators.note: first places the a and key ahead of the word It

parts.note: D is a musical key
taken as written

explanation.surface: A door that can only be opened with a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' joins: IT needs A and D placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal entrance into a mine is an opening in the hillside.

clue.text: Attack by a saint about one who became one

indicators.note: about wraps the abbreviation for saint round the next piece

parts.note: Saul of Tarsus became Saint Paul after his conversion

explanation.surface: An attack by a saint on a fellow who later became a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'saint': Saul turned into St Paul.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent physical onslaught on someone.

clue.text: Get into debts without interest

parts.note: to incur debts is to get into them
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: Borrowing money that charges no interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' looks financial but means curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking curiosity is having no interest in things.

clue.text: Deceive and attract scorn

parts.note: to con is to swindle or deceive
to tempt is to entice or attract

explanation.surface: A trickster's lure invites derision.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain and derision are synonyms of the noun.

clue.text: School batting first with cricket, say

indicators.note: first puts batting ahead of school

parts.note: a batsman batting is in
a school of thought is a sect

explanation.surface: A school team bats first in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' looks like the sport, but it is the chirping bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is an example of a six-legged creature, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Company car

definitions.meaning: someone who keeps you company, a companion or chaperone
a Ford model sold in Britain from 1968

explanation.surface: A company car, a perk of the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion keeping someone company, and a well-known Ford hatchback model.

clue.text: Beats in child's game, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word sounding alike is spoken

parts.note: conkers is a British playground game of smashing horse chestnuts on strings

explanation.surface: Someone always wins at a playground game.
explanation.walkthrough: CONKERS is a British children's game in which players swing horse chestnuts on strings at each other's.
explanation.definitionFit: To defeat or overcome an opponent is to beat them.

clue.text: Writer, a good man, seen inside foreign restaurant

indicators.note: seen inside puts the good man within the writer

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, something that writes
ST, saint, is a crossword stand-in for a good man

explanation.surface: An author and a decent fellow spotted dining abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like an author but is a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A small French-style eatery is a type of restaurant of foreign origin.

clue.text: Gets bigger, though all screwed up

definitions.meaning: grows, rises in size or amount

explanation.surface: Something swells even though it is crumpled.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN CREASES, the word describes crumpled paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Grows larger, and split in two it means full of folds and wrinkles.

clue.text: Medical treatment in battle

explanation.surface: Surgery carried out on a battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery is called this, and so is a planned military action.

clue.text: Key mixture

definitions.meaning: the key to a problem, its answer
a chemical blend dissolved in liquid

explanation.definitionFit: The answer to a puzzle, and a liquid in which something is dissolved.

clue.text: Calamity — can't dice bananas

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters of can't dice are jumbled

explanation.surface: A disaster in the kitchen: no way to chop bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit but is slang for crazy, rearranging CANT DICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap or unfortunate event is a calamity on a smaller scale.

clue.text: One extremely behind schedule is cut off

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
so means very or extremely
late means overdue

explanation.surface: A very delayed traveller is stranded.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate or set apart is to cut off from others.

clue.text: Flood discloses gold in river

indicators.note: in places gold inside the river

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A flood washes gold out from the river bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The TRENT is a long river in central England.
explanation.definitionFit: A rushing deluge of water is a flood.

clue.text: Strain to find way about the ship

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
re means about or concerning
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Struggling to find a route round the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressure or tension is strain.

clue.text: Met king, head of new nation

parts.note: R, for rex, is a king, placed as head of the remade word

indicators.note: new tells us the word nation is remade in fresh order

explanation.surface: A king leading a newly founded country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges NATION into ANINTO.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump into someone by chance is to have met them.

clue.text: Elegant braid one may make

indicators.note: the letters of braid one may make another word when reshaped

explanation.surface: A smart braid that anyone could make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may make' rearranges BRAID ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Suave, stylish and charming means elegant.

clue.text: A loose relation

parts.note: to loose a knot is to untie it

explanation.surface: A relative of loose morals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' looks like an adjective but is the verb to unfasten.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar name for a parent's sister, a family relation.

clue.text: Examination necessitating a lot of bookwork

definitions.text: Examination necessitating a lot of bookwork

parts.words: Examination necessitating a lot of bookwork
parts.note: an exam requiring revision is really a check of a firm's account books

explanation.surface: A test that needs a great deal of studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bookwork' suggests revision, but the books are financial accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: An official inspection of financial records is an examination of the books.

clue.text: She shows anger with heartless nurse

parts.note: ire is anger

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle of nurse, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A furious nurse with no compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' keeps only N and E of NURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so a 'she'.

clue.text: African soldier to request change of air

parts.note: to ask is to request

indicators.note: change of reorders the letters of air

explanation.surface: A soldier in Africa asks for fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' rearranges AIR into ARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Locally recruited troops in East Africa were known by this Swahili word for soldier.

clue.text: Cut short acrimony — compromise

parts.note: to cut something short is to end it
bitterness, anger

explanation.surface: Stop the bickering and meet halfway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compromise' looks like agreement but means to put at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise safety is to put it in peril.

clue.text: Land in Paris (Le Bourget)

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit within the words Paris and Le

explanation.surface: Touching down in Paris at Le Bourget airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' looks like an aircraft arriving, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is a piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Out to make one uneasy?

definitions.meaning: away from one's house, so unavailable to callers
ill at ease, uncomfortable in a setting

explanation.surface: Is being away from home enough to unsettle someone?
explanation.definitionFit: Absent from one's house, and also feeling ill at ease somewhere unfamiliar.
